records.name: Over the Goal Women Business Academy

schedule.text: Seven-week program. The site does not list calendar dates for the current course.

records.name: Philly Truce Foundation
records.summary: A nonprofit that runs Peace Patrol, a neighborhood safety team that hires men who were involved in the justice system, including people coming home from prison. It also holds a community parade and games.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer through the form on the site, or apply for a Peace Patrol job. Volunteers help make neighborhoods safer and support people coming home from prison.

cost.text: Volunteering has no fee. The site also asks for optional donations.

first_step.how: Fill out the volunteer form linked on phillytruce.com, or call 267-458-7823 to ask about Peace Patrol work.
first_step.basis: The site has a clear volunteer sign-up open to the public, though it does not say what a shift involves.

records.notes: Newest dated item is the July 4, 2025 Brotherly Action Parade and Games. The Peace Patrol calendar link shows no dates, and the press items are undated. The mission centers African American men and returning citizens. The volunteer form states no limit, so confirm the community tags before going live. The site lists no group email.

records.name: Team Keep
records.summary: A nonprofit that helps Philadelphia residents get back the ID papers they need for housing, jobs, benefits, and health care. It runs weekly clinics at Free Library branches.
records.what_you_do: Bring a mailing address to a clinic, where staff help you request birth certificates, photo IDs, and Social Security cards. Staff also run a phone and text hotline.

schedule.text: Weekly community clinics at six Free Library of Philadelphia branches. The clinic calendar on keep.id lists the days and places.

cost.text: Not stated in the page text.

first_step.how: Find a clinic date on the keep.id clinic calendar and bring a mailing address, or call 1-844-KEEPID with questions.
first_step.basis: The clinics are open to the public, and the site gives a phone line to ask questions.

records.name: We Love to Give
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that gives out groceries, meals, clothing, and hygiene items to neighbors facing hunger or housing trouble, and keeps a community fridge stocked.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer at a grocery giveaway, a Love Park feeding, or a community fridge refill, or donate food. People in need can come to the giveaways.

schedule.text: Grocery giveaway at Beloved St. John on the 2nd and 4th Saturdays, 12 to 1 pm. Love Park feedings on the 1st and 3rd Saturdays, noon to 1 pm or until the food runs out, weather permitting. Community fridge refilled on the 15th of each month.

cost.text: The giveaways and servings are free.

first_step.how: Come to a Saturday grocery giveaway at Beloved St. John (2nd or 4th Saturday, 12 to 1 pm), or email give@welovetogive.org to ask how to volunteer.
first_step.basis: The giveaways serve people in need, and the site gives an email address for volunteers.

notes: Fetch results came through a page summarizer, so contact details and dates should be spot-checked before anything goes live. Verdicts: 13 publish, 1 hide (P Michael Boone Foundation, private, placeholder site), 1 out_of_area (Rainbow Reserve Project, Arizona). Four publish records are held back with no summary because nothing usable was found: Roots of Justice Inc (website domain does not resolve with or without www), Times of Refreshing (website field is a publisher name, not a URL), Trina Antoinette Adams Center for Keeping Children First and Organization for Africans with Disabilities (one search each, no matching group found). The two searches went to the two IRS groups with no web address that seemed most joinable, so Roots of Justice and Times of Refreshing were not searched and the search cap of 2 is fully spent. No rate limiting, no bot checks, no 403s; the only fetch failures were the Roots of Justice domain (DNS). Over the Goal Women Business Academy is dormant (newest dated item is fall 2023). Team Keep, We Love to Give and Resolve Philly are current. Eleven of the 15 batch groups had a working website that was read (one of them, P Michael Boone, is only a placeholder); Roots of Justice had a dead domain, and the other three had no web address.
